final.memo:
Colgate-Palmolive remains a high-quality global franchise, yet it is currently a conglomerate where the high-growth Hill’s Pet Nutrition business is obscured by the broader consumer portfolio [D01, D07]. The market continues to overlook the distinct growth profile of this asset, leaving the company trading at a valuation that fails to reflect a proper sum-of-the-parts [D01]. We see a clear path to value creation by separating the business and addressing operational inefficiencies.

Our analysis suggests an implied enterprise value of $76.8bn, or $92 per share, based on a separation of Hill's at a 22x EBITDA multiple versus a more conservative 18x for the core oral and personal care franchises [D04]. This valuation is supported by an underlying 3.9% FCF yield, providing a solid floor at approximately $65 per share even in the event of a market downturn [D04].

Beyond structural complexity, the company suffers from a 270bp operating margin gap relative to Procter & Gamble, a performance delta that is untenable for a firm of this quality [D06, D07]. With a 220bp gross margin decline reported in Q3 2022, it is evident that management must move beyond incremental fixes to address persistent inflationary pressures [D03].

We have initiated a private dialogue with CEO Noel Wallace to urge a strategic review of the Hill’s business and the implementation of an aggressive operational plan to align margins with best-in-class peers [D01, D06]. Our role is one of constructive engagement, though we are prepared to escalate to a public campaign by Q2 2023 should management choose to ignore the clear value unlock available to shareholders [D01, D06].

We are sizing this position at 7% of NAV, reflecting our high conviction in the asset quality and the clarity of the catalyst [D04, D05]. We have complemented our common equity position with index hedges to mitigate the risk of broader consumer staple volatility while we execute our engagement plan [D03, D05, D08].
